results.title: Exhibition: A Life Composed: Chin Whai's Journey Through Music, Literature & Charity
results.description:
Born Tan Leng Gek (陈龙玉) (1938 – ), Chin Whai (秦淮) rose to prominence in the 1970s, when his songs captured the hearts of audiences across Singapore, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. Known for his distinctive vocal style and deeply expressive ballads, he became affectionately known as the “King of Ballads”.

Yet, long before he took to the stage as a singer, Chin Whai began his career as a writer, with works appearing in publications such as Sin Chew Daily and Nanyang Siang Pau. He published his first book at the age of 22 and went on to produce 11 volumes of poetry, prose and essays. A prolific and versatile creative, he also explored the visual arts as a painter and illustrator.

After stepping away from the spotlight, Chin Whai devoted himself to giving back to society. Over the years, he headlined numerous charity events, using his music to raise funds and support those in need. His enduring commitment to philanthropy earned him another affectionate title—the “Charity King of Songs”.

Part of NUS Libraries Chinese Popular Culture Collection series, this exhibition celebrates the the multifaceted creative life and enduring legacy of Chin Whai through a selection of materials from his private papers, generously donated to NUS Libraries. Bringing together his writings, artwork, photographs and other personal materials, the exhibition offers a glimpse into the many facets of an artist whose creative journey has spanned music, literature and the visual arts.

results.title: Exhibition: Youth, Hope & Unity: Reflections on Pope Francis's Historic Visit to Singapore
results.description:
This exhibition documents His Holiness Pope Francis' visit to Singapore in September 2024 as part of his Asia-Pacific tour – including his address at the National University of Singapore's University Cultural Centre.

Featuring objects, photographs, video footage, and printed materials from the occasion, the display centres on the hand-crafted chairs used by Pope Francis and President Tharman Shanmugaratnam during the event.

The exhibition also presents replay footage of the Pope's address, selected publications from the Library's collection, and a section highlighting student-led interfaith initiatives at NUS.

results.title: RU+ The Art & Wisdom of Lantern Riddles 灯谜慧聚：探索谜语里的智慧
results.description:
The programme will be conducted primarily in Mandarin, as Chinese lantern riddles are rooted in the Chinese language. A small number of riddles may incorporate English answers or bilingual wordplay where appropriate. AI translation in English will be provided.

Think you can crack a riddle? Try this:
At every end of a trial lies the beginning of a journey.
(Hint: An item you can find in a library)
Answer: A Journal

Did you get it right? If you enjoyed this one or found yourself scratching your head, then this programme is just for you, because we have plenty more Chinese lantern riddles (灯谜) to put your skills to the test. 😇

Join us for an interactive talk that unveils clever techniques for cracking riddles. Then, test your skills in a lively riddle-guessing activity. Work with your team to solve riddles, boost your creativity and sharpen your thinking. Along the way, learn to appreciate the wisdom of Chinese culture and language, as each lantern riddle reveals hidden meanings and ingenious wordplay.

A great op-paw-tunity to purr-fect our cat puns! 😻
results.more_info:
About the Speakers:

Ng Yok Lan is the President of the Riddle Association (Singapore). She has been instrumental in promoting lantern riddles through organizing national competitions, editing publications and spearheading outreach initiatives. She is the Chief Editor of 谜岛丛书 Volumes II, IV and V, one of the Association's key lantern riddle publications. She has also fostered exchanges with overseas experts and is committed to nurturing the next generation of lantern riddle enthusiasts through workshops, competitions and public event, helping to preserve and promote the art of lantern riddles in Singapore and beyond.

Chow Chai Khim has served in the Library for over 15 years. As a Special Collection librarian, she is dedicated to promoting rare and special collections and supporting students and researchers in discovering related Chinese and English resources—particularly in the areas of Chinese Studies and Southeast Asian Studies. She also provides information services and develops engagement programmes. In her free time, Chai Khim enjoys reading and taking leisurely strolls with her toddlers around the neighbourhood.
